text(await tools.apply_patch("*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: /tmp/exposed-tracking-fixture-design/b.md
+## Candidate B: Separate analytics fixture export
+
+## Usage (caller's view)
+```ts
+// entity-details.spec.ts and all ordinary browser specs remain unchanged.
+import { expect, test } from "./backend";
+test("browser traffic stays inside Kit", async ({ page }) => { /* existing */ });
+
+// search-tracking.spec.ts changes only its fixture import.
+import { expect, analyticsTest as test } from "./backend";
+test("each executed search emits one event", async ({ backend, page }) => {
+  // Existing capture route and analytics assertions remain here.
+});
+```
+
+## Problem
+`backend.ts` currently injects a fake token and external host into every worker's
+application process. Its default page route fulfills those external requests but
+the entity-details request listener still sees them, violating same-origin checks.
+Ordinary app workers must disable analytics, including inherited production env.
+
+## Shape
+Keep both exports in backend.ts; avoid a new module or public factory.
+```ts
+type Application = { url: string; backend: Backend };
+type AnalyticsMode = "disabled" | "capture";
+
+// Private factory: creates a distinct worker fixture definition for each export.
+function createApplicationTest(mode: AnalyticsMode) {
+  // TODO: existing base.extend<{ backend: Backend }, { application: Application }>.
+  // Existing application lifecycle, backend, and baseURL stay together here.
+  // Spawn env spreads process.env FIRST, then overrides:
+  // disabled => PUBLIC_POSTHOG_PROJECT_TOKEN: "", PUBLIC_POSTHOG_HOST: ""
+  // capture => fake token and https://posthog.test.
+  // No general page override here.
+  throw new Error("not implemented");
+}
+export const test = createApplicationTest("disabled");
+export const analyticsTest = createApplicationTest("capture").extend({
+  page: async ({ page }, use) => {
+    await page.route("https://posthog.test/**", route => route.fulfill({ json: {} }));
+    await use(page);
+  },
+});
+```
+Distinct application fixture definitions prevent worker reuse across modes.
+Current workerIndex-based ports remain sufficient for separate Playwright workers.
+Only analyticsTest installs the fake-host safety route; the spec's later route
+continues capturing payloads using Playwright's latest-handler-first semantics.
+One module owns startup, teardown, mode env, and interception defaults; callers
+select a complete fixture using one import, per boundary-discipline.
+
+## Tradeoffs accepted
+- A second named export makes selection explicit; no new test.use option exists.
+- A tiny private factory avoids duplicating the process lifecycle, at the cost of
+  indenting the existing fixture definition and starting distinct mode workers.
+
+## Alternatives considered
+A worker-scoped option on the shared fixture needs fewer exports, but exposes mode
+configuration to every spec and relies on each analytics caller setting it.
+A separate module would need an exported factory or duplicated lifecycle; neither
+improves the isolation provided by distinct fixture exports here.
+
+## Synthesis decision and implementation reconciliation
+Pending parent comparison; no repository implementation performed.
+
+## Verification and next implementation step
+Implement the private factory and switch the tracking import; run tracking and
+the entity-details same-origin test together, then the existing browser suite.
+Inspect ordinary-worker env to ensure inherited real credentials are overridden.
*** End Patch"));
